beats.text: Before clocks, the only timekeeper was the sun.
Over three thousand years ago, Egyptians read the time from moving shadows.
But shadows vanish at night, so water clocks dripped at a steady rate to mark the hours.
Medieval Europe built giant tower clocks, driven by falling weights and gears.
In 1656, Christiaan Huygens added a pendulum, and clocks finally became accurate.
In 1969, the first quartz watch arrived. Its tiny crystal vibrates over thirty-two thousand times a second.
Today, atomic clocks lose less than a second in millions of years, and they keep GPS on time.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
